name: Black Ram Exchange
summary: Black Ram Exchange is a simple transaction handled by Veron Amberstill at the Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh. It allows riders who hold an older, unarmored Black Ram mount to trade it in for a newer breed favored across the Alliance. It reflects the ongoing stewardship and breeding practices of Ironforge's foremost mount breeders.

sections.title: Tending the Herd
sections.body: The Amberstill Ranch, nestled in the snowy valleys of Dun Morogh northeast of Kharanos, is the heart of dwarven mount breeding. Veron Amberstill manages the stout mountain rams that have carried Ironforge mountaineers across craggy peaks for generations. When changes in mount training and regional saddle standards began spreading through the Alliance, Veron took charge of handling direct exchanges for riders wishing to update their stables.

sections.title: A Rare Breed
sections.body: The original Black Ram represents an earlier generation of mountain stock—prized for its rugged stamina and dark fleece. As dwarven breeders introduced newer barding and standardized breeds to better equip Alliance champions, Veron agreed to take back these older mounts in trade, ensuring that veteran riders were not left behind as stable practices evolved.

faq.q: What is the Black Ram Exchange?
faq.answer: It is a straightforward trade offered by Veron Amberstill at the Amberstill Ranch. Adventurers who possess an older, swift Black Ram can turn it over to him in exchange for a modernized mount of comparable prestige.

Veron Amberstill is the master ram breeder of Dun Morogh, based at the Amberstill Ranch. He is responsible for raising, breaking, and selling rams to the Alliance, serving as the primary mount vendor for the dwarven people.

faq.q: Where does this exchange take place?
aliases: where to turn in black ram
faq.answer: The exchange occurs at Amberstill Ranch, located northeast of Kharanos and just south of the main road leading east toward Loch Modan in Dun Morogh.

faq.q: Why were older rams traded in?
faq.answer: Breeders and stable masters across Azeroth began retiring older, unarmored swift mounts in favor of standard breeds fitted with armor and tailored harness gear. The Amberstills offered this exchange so veteran riders could adopt the newer breeds if they chose.

faq.q: Can any Alliance hero trade with Veron Amberstill?
faq.answer: While dwarf adventurers are natural ram riders, heroes from other Alliance races who have earned high renown with Ironforge and acquired the appropriate riding skill can also ride and trade these mountain beasts.

faq.q: Do I have to trade my old Black Ram?
faq.answer: No. The exchange is entirely voluntary. Riders who prefer the classic, unarmored appearance of the original Black Ram are free to keep their trusty mount.

angles.text: For the dwarves of Khaz Modan, rams are not merely beasts of burden, but symbols of mountain pride raised carefully by the Amberstills in Dun Morogh.
Alliance heroes who gain the trust of the Ironforge dwarves can ride these sure-footed mountain rams, provided they have mastered the necessary riding discipline.
